name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,634

clue.text: Break from wearing corsets?

blocks.note: surface reading: some relief from having to lace yourself into tight underwear
setter's reading: a holiday spent at home, punning on stays, the old word for corsets

explanation.walkthrough: Stays are an old name for a corset, so the clue pretends the holiday is a rest from them; really it is a break taken without leaving home.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday spent at home rather than travelling away is a recent coinage blending two everyday words.

clue.text: Torment me on the radio?

indicators.note: radio is heard rather than read, so we want a word that sounds like the one meant

blocks.note: the setter of this puzzle is Tees, so 'me' is the setter's own name

explanation.surface: Someone challenges a broadcaster to pick on them over the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: In cryptics 'me' often stands for the setter; this puzzle is by Tees, whose name is pronounced the same as the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester or mock someone playfully is a mild way of tormenting them; both are verbs.

clue.text: Outbreak of cowardice?

blocks.note: surface reading: a sudden wave of people losing their nerve
setter's reading: an epidemic of a tropical disease whose colour name also means lacking courage

explanation.walkthrough: Cowardice is called yellow, and an outbreak is what a disease has; together they name a viral illness spread by mosquitoes.
explanation.definitionFit: This mosquito-borne tropical disease causes jaundice, and its colour word is slang for being timid.

clue.text: Gangster on his own without detonator

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece stands around another

blocks.note: someone on their own is by themselves
a percussion cap is a small detonating charge

explanation.surface: A mobster working solo has no means of setting off his bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', which suits the surface, but here it means 'outside', the older sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chicago crime boss of the Prohibition era is the archetypal American mobster of the 1920s.

clue.text: Sharing soapy water on getting into it together?

indicators.note: one thing getting into another ends up placed inside it

blocks.note: two people sharing the suds are in one tub
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A couple climbing into the tub together and sharing the bathwater.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole first phrase reads as part of the picture, but it is a full piece, IN THE SAME BATH, which takes RE inside its last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying two things almost simultaneously, one right after the other, is an idiom for doing them at the same time.

clue.text: Pot knocked over — family needs serviette

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so in a down clue the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a cooking pot
one's relatives

explanation.surface: A saucepan has been tipped over at dinner and the family needs something to mop up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the reversal reads upwards, which suits 'knocked over' as a picture of a pot tipped on its side.
explanation.definitionFit: Serviette is the British word for the cloth or paper square used to wipe your mouth at table.

clue.text: One might pick this rugby forward

blocks.note: first meaning: a burglar picks a door fastening open
second meaning: a second-row player in the scrum

explanation.surface: A selector deciding which forward to choose for the rugby team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick' suggests choosing a player, but it is the burglar's sort of picking. In rugby union the two locks bind in the second row of the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a key-operated fastening that thieves pick and a tall forward position in rugby.

clue.text: Deep Blue

blocks.note: first meaning: of a sound or voice, bass in pitch
second meaning: sad, down in spirits

explanation.walkthrough: Deep Blue reads as the chess-playing IBM computer, or a dark shade; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers a bass pitch of voice and a dejected, gloomy mood.

clue.text: Winger wrecked motor car touring north

indicators.note: a wrecked vehicle is smashed up, so these letters are broken and rebuilt
to tour is to go all round something, so one piece encircles another

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A footballer on the wing crashed his car while driving in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer, but in crosswords it is often a bird, a thing with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: This large dark fish-eating seabird flies, so it is a creature with wings.

clue.text: Girl corrupted round adult clubs: item for the press?

definitions.note: a cryptic definition by way of the kitchen press

indicators.note: something corrupted has been spoilt and altered, so the letters are rearranged
to go round something is to enclose it

blocks.note: taken as written
A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A tabloid story about a girl led astray by grown-up nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The press' suggests newspapers, matching the scandal; it is the kitchen gadget that crushes cloves.
explanation.definitionFit: A garlic press is a kitchen tool for crushing cloves, so the bulb is what you put in one.

clue.text: Parasite in record dispute sent back millions

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to record is to tape
a row is a quarrel
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A bloodsucking figure caught up in a record-breaking contract row that cost millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but it only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This long flat worm lives inside the gut of its host, a classic intestinal parasite.

clue.text: Japanese fighter gives you nothing

blocks.note: first meaning: the Mitsubishi warplane of the Second World War
second meaning: the number nought

explanation.surface: A Japanese boxer or soldier who refuses to give you anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighter' sounds like a person, but it is the wartime fighter aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the famous carrier-based warplane is also the word for the figure nought.

clue.text: Mimicking bird, cat who looks for excitement?

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'one who looks for excitement'

blocks.note: imitating a small bird's call, a peep
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A cat chirping like a bird to stir up a little thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'looks': a voyeur literally looks, for a thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: A voyeur spies on others for sexual gratification, someone who seeks a thrill by watching.

clue.text: Large singer dressed in Scots headgear

indicators.note: dressing something rearranges and prepares it, as a chef dresses a crab

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A big vocalist turns up in Highland caps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed in' reads as wearing, but 'dressed' is the anagram signal and 'in' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: These boat-shaped woollen caps with ribbons at the back are traditional Highland military bonnets.

clue.text: Orchestra to transgress, less authentic for an audience?

indicators.note: an audience hears a performance, so the word is chosen for its sound

blocks.note: to sin is to break a moral law
phonier means more fake

explanation.surface: An orchestra cheating by miming its performance in front of the listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the comparative of phoney ends without an R sound, so it matches the last part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinfonia is Italian for symphony and is used in the names of chamber orchestras.

clue.text: One can rave about European wandering

indicators.note: about means around, so the pieces wrap around another

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a tin is a can
to rant is to rave
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A person enthusing about a roaming continental traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One can' reads as a pronoun and verb, but both are nouns here.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerant describes someone who travels from place to place without settling, as roving people do.

clue.text: Value returned welcoming a Biblical brother

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards
to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: use is value, as in 'of no use'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A family brother who comes back, valued and welcomed home.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal happens first; the single letter then sits inside the turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis he is Jacob's twin, who sold his birthright for a bowl of stew.

clue.text: Certain people cannot be so described

definitions.text: Certain people cannot be so described

blocks.note: surface reading: some particular people who must not be described a certain way
setter's reading: people who are sure cannot be called the opposite of sure

explanation.walkthrough: 'Certain people' looks like 'some people'; read it as 'people who are certain' and the answer is the word that contradicts them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unsure is the opposite of being confident, so a confident person cannot be called it.

clue.text: Kevin shortly consuming one chicken dish

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so one piece takes another inside

blocks.note: the familiar short form of the name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man called Kevin quickly eating a chicken dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' looks like 'soon', but it tells you to use the clipped form of the name; KEV is the usual British nickname for Kevin.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken Kiev is a breaded fillet stuffed with garlic butter, named after the Ukrainian capital.

clue.text: Stretch out scandal involving Mister Musk?

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or include, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: the first name of the tech billionaire
-gate is the suffix tacked onto scandals since Watergate

explanation.surface: A drawn-out controversy surrounding Elon Musk.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the container wraps the name entirely at the front: the scandal word sits after it, so the result reads as a plain join.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen something is to draw it out, so the verb pair are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Position figures around university

indicators.note: around means on all sides, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: stats is short for statistics, numerical figures
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Rankings and statistics that decide where a university stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' could be people or shapes; here it means numbers, clipped to their informal short form.
explanation.definitionFit: One's standing or rank in society or an organisation is one's social position.

clue.text: Both rather drunk, fans may swoon over him

definitions.note: a clause standing for the noun 'one fans swoon over'

indicators.note: a drunk person is unsteady and muddled, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Two tipsy admirers ready to faint over a handsome star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rather drunk' looks like a degree of intoxication; 'rather' is fodder and 'drunk' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome male celebrity who makes admirers go weak at the knees is a pin-up idol.

clue.text: Duck takes sheep outside for wander

indicators.note: a piece placed outside another surrounds it

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, which looks like the letter O
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A duck leading a sheep out of the field for a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a batsman's score of nought, hence the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To rove or drift about without a fixed destination is the same as meandering aimlessly.

clue.text: Craftsman on the fiddle a dull one

blocks.note: taken as written
mat is a variant spelling of matt, not shiny
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A tradesman doing something crooked, and boring with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the fiddle' suggests cheating; it means working on violins.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amati family of Cremona were celebrated violin makers, teachers of the tradition Stradivari followed.

clue.text: All for end in feud in Maltese capital

indicators.note: one thing given for another is swapped in its place

blocks.note: a vendetta is a long-running feud
taken as written, the letters removed
taken as written, the letters put in

explanation.surface: Everyone caught up in a deadly quarrel in Malta's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End in feud' reads as the last letter of feud, but it is the literal word END found inside a synonym for feud.
explanation.definitionFit: Valletta is the fortified harbour city that serves as the capital of Malta.

clue.text: Room for experimentation in alcohol abuse

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words, spanning the gap between them

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A place where people try out drinking to excess.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like a place for trying out vices, which suits the surface; it is simply a science room, its name shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory is a room equipped for scientific tests, shortened in everyday speech.

clue.text: One died in fight — but when?

definitions.note: an adverbial question standing for a day

indicators.note: in means placed inside something else

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
a fray is a fight or brawl

explanation.surface: Someone was killed in a brawl, but the date is unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But when?' reads as a detective's follow-up question; the definition is just 'when?', answered by a day of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: A weekday is a possible reply to a question asking at what time something happened.

clue.text: Go mad when retired

indicators.note: retiring is withdrawing or going back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Someone going crazy once they stop working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb about becoming; it is the noun meaning an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a go at something and having a stab at it are idioms for making an attempt.

clue.text: Pedant and stoic clash explosively

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, scattering the letters into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nitpicker and a stern philosopher having a furious row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedant' could be part of the scene; the anagram is of the last two words only.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a scholastic is a medieval schoolman, and by extension a hair-splitting academic.
